title: KYC (regulated countries)
content:
# KYC (regulated countries)

Collect the identity details a regulated country requires, submit them with POST /v1/phone-numbers/kyc or a hosted link, and fix a declined number.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

By the end of this page, a number in a regulated country is in regulatory review under your team. You also know how to fix it if the reviewer declines it.

## Before you start

You need a profile id and a [purchase](/platforms/phone-numbers/setup#step-2-purchase) that returned `status: "kyc_required"`.

The US provisions numbers instantly. Other countries regulate who can hold a number and need the registrant's identity before the number is ordered.

That `202` also carries a `kycUrl`, a ready-made link to the [hosted form](#hand-the-form-off-white-label) for the country. Use it to hand the step off instead of building the form with the endpoints below.

## Step 1: Check availability and the address constraint

Call `GET /v1/phone-numbers/availability` with `country`. It tells you whether deliverable inventory exists and which address the registrant needs:

- `geo`: the address must be in one of the returned `areas` (some countries stock numbers tied to a city).
- `country`: any in-country address works.
- `none`: no address is required.

[Availability and pricing](/platforms/phone-numbers/availability#check-one-country) has the call and its response.

Checking first avoids the worst case: a submission that passes review but can never be assigned a number, because the address is in the wrong area.

### Out of stock? Pre-order it

When `available` is `false` but `preOrderable` is `true`, you can still order the number. Run the same KYC flow below: the submission places a pre-order.

We then get the number the fastest way available. That is regular stock the moment it comes back, otherwise a number the carrier sources for this registration.

Sourcing usually takes 2 to 4 weeks and is not guaranteed.

**One area.** A sold-out area listed in `soldOutAreas` with `preOrderable: true` works the same way. Pre-order it by sending its `ndc` as `areaCode` with `preOrder: true`.

**Geo countries.** In a country with `addressConstraint: "geo"` (the number's area code must cover the registered address), the area comes from the address.

When the address you submit sits in an area we have no stock in, the first submit creates nothing. It answers `409` with `code: "area_pre_order_available"`.

The carrier can source a number there, but the customer should agree to the wait first. The `error` message is ready to show as is. `details` carries:

- `areaCode`
- `areaName`
- `estimatedWeeks` (`"2-4"`)
- `billedWhenActive: true`

Once they agree, resend the same body with `preOrder: true`. Adding `details.areaCode` as `areaCode` is optional. The pre-order is placed for exactly that area.

- The submit response carries `preOrder: true`, and the number stays `pending_regulatory` until it is sourced.
- Nothing is billed until the number is active. If the carrier cannot source it, the number is declined with a reason (the usual [`whatsapp.number.declined`](/webhooks/whatsapp/whatsapp-number-declined) webhook) and nothing was charged.
- A pre-order is one number per submission, so `quantity` must be 1.
- To cancel, release the number (`DELETE /v1/phone-numbers/{id}`) while it is still pending. We withdraw the carrier request too, so nothing is charged.
- Only countries and types that require KYC can be pre-ordered. That includes types marked `fulfilment: "request"` by `listPhoneNumberCountries` (`GET /v1/phone-numbers/countries`), which the carrier stocks nowhere and only sources to order. `preOrderable` on each type tells you which ones qualify.

## Step 2: Get the form for the country

Call `GET /v1/phone-numbers/kyc` with `country`. It returns the fields the country requires, and whether your team already holds a reusable, approved verification for that country.

Requirements and reuse eligibility are per country and number type. Add `numberType` when you want something other than the country's default, and send the same value on the submit.

A field's `kind` is one of:

- `text`
- `date`
- `address`
- `file` (an ID or a business registration)
- `action`, an out-of-band identity verification run by Onfido

An `action` field is not filled in on this form. It is fulfilled after the order, through a link, in [step 4](#step-4-forward-the-id-verification-link).

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();
const profileId = '66a1f0c2a4b9d3e8f1a2b3c4';

const { data: form } = await zernio.phonenumbers.getPhoneNumberKycForm({
  query: { country: 'GB' }
});
for (const f of form.fields) {
  console.log(f.requirementId, f.kind, f.label);
}
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()
profile_id = "66a1f0c2a4b9d3e8f1a2b3c4"

form = client.phone_numbers.get_phone_number_kyc_form(country="GB")
for f in form["fields"]:
    print(f["requirementId"], f["kind"], f["label"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/phone-numbers/kyc?country=GB" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "country": "GB",
  "numberType": "local",
  "fields": [
    { "requirementId": "d7e8f9a0-b1c2-4d3e-9f4a-5b6c7d8e9f0a", "label": "Business name", "kind": "text", "example": "Acme Ltd" },
    { "requirementId": "e8f9a0b1-c2d3-4e4f-8a5b-6c7d8e9f0a1b", "label": "Proof of identity", "kind": "file", "description": "Passport or ID card, both sides" },
    { "requirementId": "f9a0b1c2-d3e4-4f5a-9b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c", "label": "Business address", "kind": "address", "localTo": "GB" }
  ],
  "reusable": null,
  "pendingReview": false
}
```

When `reusable` is set, submit with `reuse: true` and the option's `id` as `reuseOptionId`. That skips the documents, and the order is placed at once.

## Step 3: Submit the details

Call `POST /v1/phone-numbers/kyc` with `profileId`, `country`, and the `values`, `documents` and `address` keyed by `requirementId`.

- Repeat the `numberType` from step 2 to order that type.
- Add `wantsSms: true` to have SMS enabled on activation. This draws the order from SMS-capable stock.

Send each document inline as base64. Or upload it first with `POST /v1/phone-numbers/kyc/upload-document` (raw bytes, filename in `X-Filename`) and pass the returned `documentId`.

<Callout type="warn">For an ID-card requirement, carriers need both sides. Combine front and back into one file before uploading: a one-sided ID is a common decline reason.</Callout>

**ID verification.** Add `endUserFirstName` and `endUserLastName` when the form returned a field with `kind: "action"`. The country's ID-verification step needs the end user's legal name, and the submit is rejected without it.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/phone-numbers/kyc" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "profileId": "66a1f0c2a4b9d3e8f1a2b3c4",
    "country": "GB",
    "values": { "d7e8f9a0-b1c2-4d3e-9f4a-5b6c7d8e9f0a": "Acme Ltd" },
    "documents": [{ "requirementId": "e8f9a0b1-c2d3-4e4f-8a5b-6c7d8e9f0a1b", "filename": "id.pdf", "base64": "JVBERi0xLjQK..." }],
    "address": {
      "requirementId": "f9a0b1c2-d3e4-4f5a-9b6c-7d8e9f0a1b2c", "country_code": "GB",
      "street_address": "10 Downing Street", "locality": "London",
      "administrative_area": "London", "postal_code": "SW1A 2AA"
    }
  }'
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "status": "kyc_submitted",
  "phoneNumber": {
    "id": "66d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4",
    "status": "pending_regulatory",
    "country": "GB"
  },
  "numbers": [
    { "id": "66d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4", "status": "pending_regulatory", "phoneNumber": null, "country": "GB" }
  ]
}
```

The order goes to regulatory review. The number activates within 1 to 3 business days.

Poll `GET /v1/phone-numbers/{id}`, or listen for [`whatsapp.number.activated`](/webhooks/whatsapp/whatsapp-number-activated) and [`whatsapp.number.declined`](/webhooks/whatsapp/whatsapp-number-declined). They fire for every number; the names are legacy.

**Retries.** Send a `submissionId` so a retry of the same attempt returns the same number instead of ordering another.

**Several numbers.** `quantity` (1 to 5) provisions several same-country numbers from one verification.

ID documents and the address stream straight to the number provider inside the request. Zernio never stores the document bytes.

Two optional checks run before you submit:

- `POST /v1/phone-numbers/kyc/validate-address` checks an address for deliverability before you upload anything.
- `POST /v1/phone-numbers/kyc/review-packet` reviews a whole packet for likely decline reasons.

## Step 4: Forward the ID-verification link

Only for a country whose form carried an `action` field.

Once the order is placed, `onfidoVerificationUrl` appears on the number and holds the link the end user has to complete.

It is `null` on every other number and until the order exists, so poll `GET /v1/phone-numbers/{id}` after submitting.

```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/phone-numbers/66d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```

Response (`200`), trimmed:

```json
{
  "phoneNumber": {
    "id": "66d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4",
    "status": "pending_regulatory",
    "country": "GB",
    "onfidoVerificationUrl": "https://id.onfido.app/..."
  }
}
```

Send that link to the end user. The requirement stays unmet until they finish the check.

A number whose link nobody opened sits in `pending_regulatory` past the usual 1 to 3 business days.

## Hand the form off (white-label)

Call `POST /v1/phone-numbers/kyc/share` with `profileId` and `country` when you would rather not build the document-collection UI.

It returns a single-use hosted page running the same guided wizard. The page is valid 7 days and needs no Zernio login.

- `branding` (company name, logo, brand color) puts your brand on the page. It opens with "*companyName* asked you to complete identity verification".
- `redirect_url` sends the customer back to your app afterward. Zernio appends `kyc=submitted` and `country=<ISO-2>` to it.

The number provisions under your team once they submit, and [`whatsapp.number.kyc_submitted`](/webhooks/whatsapp/whatsapp-number-kyc-submitted) fires.

**Language.** Pass `language` (`en`, `es` or `pt-BR`) to set the page's language. Its copy, the carrier's requirement texts, the pre-submit review notes and the status emails your customer receives all follow it.

Omitted, the page uses the customer's browser language when it is one of those three, else English. The customer can switch with `?lang=es` on the page URL.

Some carriers still require certain answers in English (a business use-case description, for instance). The form says so on that field.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/phone-numbers/kyc/share" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "profileId": "66a1f0c2a4b9d3e8f1a2b3c4",
    "country": "GB",
    "branding": { "companyName": "Acme", "logoUrl": "https://acme.example.com/logo.png", "brandColor": "#1a73e8" },
    "redirect_url": "https://acme.example.com/numbers/done"
  }'
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "url": "https://zernio.com/kyc/share/...",
  "token": "...",
  "expiresAt": "2027-01-08T12:00:00Z"
}
```

## Fix a declined number

You do not start over. A declined number stays in your list with status `regulatory_declined` and `regulatoryDeclineReason`.

The `status=pending_regulatory` filter on `GET /v1/phone-numbers` also surfaces numbers declined in the last 30 days.

1. Call `GET /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/remediate` for only the requirements the reviewer flagged.
2. Call `POST /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/remediate` with the corrected `values`, `documents` or `address`.

The number goes back to review on the same record. It keeps its place in the queue and is not billed again.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/phone-numbers/66d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4/remediate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"documents": [{ "requirementId": "e8f9a0b1-c2d3-4e4f-8a5b-6c7d8e9f0a1b", "filename": "id-both-sides.pdf", "base64": "JVBERi0xLjQK..." }]}'
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "status": "pending_regulatory",
  "phoneNumber": { "id": "66d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4", "status": "pending_regulatory" }
}
```

## Answer the reviewer

Not every ask fits the form. A reviewer who writes "is this a personal or a business line?" wants a sentence, and the structured requirements have nowhere to put it.

`POST /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/remediate/respond` sends one response covering both. At least one of these is required:

- a `message` to the reviewer
- corrected `documents` or `address`, when you have them
- up to 5 loose `attachments` (PDF, JPG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each), whose links are added to the message

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/phone-numbers/66d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4/remediate/respond" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "This is a business line for Acme Ltd; the utility bill is in the company name."}'
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "status": "replied",
  "posted": true,
  "phoneNumber": { "id": "66d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4", "status": "pending_regulatory" },
  "siblingsResubmitted": 0
}
```

`status` is `replied` for a message-only response. It is `resubmitted` when corrections went with it, which is also what moves the number back into review.

`siblingsResubmitted` counts the other numbers on the same registration the correction fanned out to.

`POST /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/remediate/reply` is the message-only half of the same job, taking `text` and `attachments`.

**Comment or decline.** Answering a comment-style ask puts the number back in review on its own. A reply on a formal decline is supplementary, so still send the fix through `POST /v1/phone-numbers/{id}/remediate`.

**`409`.** The number sits under Zernio's own carrier registration, so there is nothing for you to correct.

## If it fails

A `400` on the submit means a value failed validation. Most often it is an address outside the country or a file over the size limit:

```json
{
  "error": "Address must be in GB",
  "type": "invalid_request_error",
  "param": "address"
}
```

Run `POST /v1/phone-numbers/kyc/validate-address` first to catch it before uploading documents.

A `409` means one of these:

- `reuse: true` was sent with no approved verification on file.
- The area covering the registered address has no inventory but can be pre-ordered once the customer agrees (`code: "area_pre_order_available"`, resend with `preOrder: true`).
- The requested `areaCode` (or that address area) has no inventory and cannot be pre-ordered (`code: "area_code_unavailable"`).
- The whole country and type has nothing deliverable and cannot be pre-ordered (`code: "country_out_of_stock"`).

**Held-back numbers.** Sometimes the only numbers the carrier lists failed WhatsApp registration recently and are held back. The message then names the date the first one clears, and `details.undeliverableUntil` carries it as an ISO timestamp.

Nothing changes before that date. Pick another area from `areaOptions` or set a [stock watch](/platforms/phone-numbers/availability#watch-an-out-of-stock-country).

Every error uses the envelope in [error handling](/guides/error-handling).
